Cautiously positive, with credit-channel nuance from SLOOS:
- Business credit: Domestic banks expect to ease standards for C&I loans and report stable-to-stronger demand in some segments, which supports the FOMC’s “moderate” growth outlook and accommodative stance. However, foreign banks anticipate tightening C&I standards and weaker business loan demand, tempering the impulse.
- Household credit: Banks expect to ease standards for several residential mortgage categories, a mild support to housing and consumption. Offsetting this, banks expect to tighten auto loan standards and foresee deteriorating asset quality in credit card and auto loans, signaling consumer-credit headwinds.
- Commercial real estate: Banks expect to tighten standards for CRE (including construction/land development and multifamily), and both domestic and foreign banks see potential deterioration in multifamily asset quality—consistent with lingering softness in business fixed investment and a more cautious risk backdrop.

Net: The FOMC’s gradualism and balanced risk assessment remain appropriate, but SLOOS indicates a mixed credit supply picture—supportive for C&I and mortgages, cautious for CRE and consumer credit—so the tone is modestly optimistic but slightly more tempered than before.
